title: Rearchitect CPU workerpool and decouple request serialization to reduce host context switches and pinning overhead
author: Eli Navarro
description: Context: production inference workloads showed increased P95 latency under moderate concurrency due to host thread preemption and lock contention in the request hot path. Root cause analysis pointed to three correlated issues: a) synchronous request serialization (protobuf/json) inside the main dispatch threads, b) a global mutex and condition-variable based worker pool that caused frequent context switches when workers were pinned/affined, and c) KV cache eviction callbacks running on the same CPU worker threads. This PR rearchitects the CPU-side request path to decouple serialization from the dispatch path, introduce per-core lock-free task queues with cooperative scheduling, and isolate KV cache maintenance off the hot workerpool. Design summary: 1) Serialization pipeline: move protobuf/json encode/decode into a bounded, pooled serialization worker set that runs at lower priority and is immune to accelerator-affinity pinning. Requests now enqueue a lightweight serialization task and immediately yield to the fast-path scheduler which only touches minimal request metadata and placement hints. 2) Workerpool redesign: replace the global mutex/condvar pool with per-core MPMC lock-free rings (based on FAA + circular buffers) and cooperative worker yielding. Workers honor affinity hints but avoid hard pinning; we now use soft-affinity + OS sched affinity hints only for Dedicated mode. 3) Cooperative scheduling and backpressure: introduce a fast-path credit system per route to enforce SLO-aware batching and avoid over-scheduling CPU workers when the GPU is saturated. 4) KV cache isolation: eviction and persistence callbacks are moved to a single-purpose maintenance pool to avoid creating tail-latency spikes on inference workers. 5) Observability: new timers around serialization enqueue/wait, workerqueue depth metrics, and an end-to-end request-span tagging to correlate heavy serialization work with latency regressions. Changes made: - runtime/worker_pool.cc: new per-core lock-free queue implementation, cooperative yield loop, worker lifecycle changes. - runtime/serialization_pool.{cc,h}: pooled serializer, buffer pool reuse, preallocated scratch buffers, lower-priority worker set. - runtime/affinity.cc: decouple hard-pinning code paths; soft affinity fallbacks per deployment mode. - runtime/kv_cache.cc: move eviction callbacks to maintenance pool and add async flush APIs. - runtime/slo_controller.cc: per-route crediting and batching guards. - benchmarks/cpu_hotpath_microbench.cc: microbench harness and synthetic test vectors. - docs/perf/workerpool.md: design and operational notes. Testing and validation: - Microbenchmarks: measured service-side P50 unchanged, P95 reduced by 30-45% depending on concurrency and model context length. - End-to-end canary: deployed to a dedicated canary fleet of 8 nodes; tail latency improvements were consistent under both short (32) and long (2048) context workloads. - Stress: ran soak 72h with burst traffic patterns and verified no regressions in throughput or memory. - CI: surfaced a flaky test in tests/workerpool/test_cooperative_yield which required timing loosening; reran full CI before merge. Rollout and compatibility: - The change is safe for backward compatibility; the soft-affinity behavior is controlled by a config flag (runtime.use_soft_affinity) defaulting to true for Dedicated and false for Hosted (to preserve historical behavior). - Migration: operators can opt into serialized-pool first via runtime.enable_serialization_pool. Observability additions included by default so regressions are visible. Related work: follows on investigation ENG-1247 and complements earlier batching improvements in ENG-998. Checklist: [x] unit tests updated [x] integration test added [x] perf microbench added [x] canary deployment validated [x] docs updated Related files and commits are listed below.

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Can you clarify the decision to use soft affinity by default in Dedicated mode? Is there a measurable downside in Hosted?

Author (Eli): Soft affinity reduces hard preemption and migration when host kernels (e.g. syscalls) spike. Hosted keeps hard-pinning off to allow container schedulers to do placement. No throughput loss seen in Hosted during canary.
Marco Ruiz: The lock-free ring looks good but add a crash-safe fallback path if the FAA loop fails under heavy contention.
Author: Added a fallback spin-compare path and documented in worker_pool.h comments and tests. Also added assertions in debug builds.
Lena Fischer: We should ensure the serialization pool respects per-tenant rate limits to avoid noisy neighbors.
Author: Serialization enqueue is accounted against the same per-route credits; updated slo_controller to include serialized tasks in accounting.
release_notes: Reduce CPU-side tail latency by redesigning workerpool and decoupling request serialization: P95 improvements 30-45% in microbenchmarks; new config toggles runtime.use_soft_affinity and runtime.enable_serialization_pool; added observability for serialization latency and workerqueue depth.
